newsitem.title: UK: S&P assigns Serail FFr 2.6 bln seven year FRN.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns Serail FFr 2.6 bln seven year FRN.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had assigned Serail Plc's FFr2.6 billion guaranteed senior floating rate notes due 2004 its AAA rating.
Serail Plc is a special purpose company incorporated in Ireland.

S&P said the deal consisted of the securitization of a portfolio of bonds issued by French corporates and financial institutions, which as of the closing date is expected to have an aggregate principal amount of FFr3.0 billion (about US$525 million).
It said the transaction represented the first Collateralized Bond Obligation (CBO) originated by a French institution, Banque Arjil & Cie S.C.A.

In assigning a triple-'A' rating to the guaranteed senior floating rate notes, Standard & Poor's said it relied primarily on the financial guaranty insurance policy to be issued by Financial Security Assurance (FSA).

"In addition, the Notes will benefit from the sound credit quality of the assets as well as the protection given by the Mezzanine Floating Rate Notes and Subordinated Floating Rate Notes that will be issued by the Issuer in an aggregate initial principal amount of FFr406 million," said S&P.
"Both the mezzanine floating rate notes and the subordinated floating rate notes will be subordinated in payment to the rated senior notes."
It said the sound legal structure of the transaction would also be an essential factor in the rating
